title: Structure and General Properties of the Metalloids
lead: The six metalloids, boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony and tellurium, stand between the metals and the nonmetals. The section looks at the covalent crystals they form, then at boron and silicon in detail: how each is found and purified, their halides as Lewis acids, boric acid and the borates, and silica and the silicates.
objectives: Describe the general preparation, properties, and uses of the metalloids
Describe the preparation, properties, and compounds of boron and silicon
summary_html: The elements boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony, and tellurium separate the metals from the nonmetals in the periodic table. These elements, called metalloids or sometimes semimetals, exhibit properties characteristic of both metals and nonmetals. The structures of these elements are similar in many ways to those of nonmetals, but the elements are electrical semiconductors.

Because carbon tends to form double and triple bonds and silicon does not, (a) carbon dioxide is a discrete molecule with two C=O double bonds and (b) silicon dioxide is an infinite network of oxygen atoms bridging between silicon atoms with each silicon atom possessing four Si-O single bonds. Describe the hybridization of silicon and the molecular structure of the following molecules and ions:
(a) (CH3)3SiH
(b) $\text{SiO}_{4}{}^{4−}$
(c) Si2H6
(d) Si(OH)4
(e) $\text{SiF}_{6}{}^{2−}$

answer.solution: (a) (CH3)3SiH: sp3 bonding about Si; the structure is tetrahedral; (b) $\text{SiO}_{4}{}^{\text{4−}}$: sp3 bonding about Si; the structure is tetrahedral; (c) Si2H6: sp3 bonding about each Si; the structure is linear along the Si-Si bond; (d) Si(OH)4: sp3 bonding about Si; the structure is tetrahedral; (e) $\text{SiF}_{6}{}^{\text{2−}}$: sp3d2 bonding about Si; the structure is octahedral

exercises.prompt: Describe the hybridization and the bonding of a silicon atom in elemental silicon.

answer.solution: Suggested approach: recall the diamond structure the text gives silicon, count the neighbors each silicon atom bonds to and the shape they make, and choose the set of hybrid orbitals that points to the corners of that shape; then say what kind of bond each hybrid orbital forms with a neighbor.

exercises.prompt: Why is boron limited to a maximum coordination number of four in its compounds?

answer.solution: Boron has only s and p orbitals available, which can accommodate a maximum of four electron pairs. Unlike silicon, no d orbitals are available in boron.

exercises.prompt: Suppose you discovered a diamond completely encased in a silicate rock. How would you chemically free the diamond without harming it?

answer.solution: A mild solution of hydrofluoric acid would dissolve the silicate and would not harm the diamond.
